summary: A month grid for picking a date or a span of them.

pairs.dont: Grey out dates and leave people guessing why.
pairs.do: Say the rule near the calendar — "data is kept for 13 months".
pairs.why: A disabled day looks the same whether it is in the past, outside a retention window or already booked. Only words separate them.

pairs.dont: Ask for a range in a single month view.
pairs.do: Show two months when the span is likely to cross one.
pairs.why: Most ranges cross a month boundary, and paging back and forth loses the first end of the selection from view.

pairs.dont: Use a calendar to capture a birth year.
pairs.do: Use a calendar for dates near today; use fields for anything far away.
pairs.why: A grid is faster than typing for this month. It is much slower than typing for 1974.

pairs.dont: Style today the same as the chosen day.
pairs.do: Keep today's subtle fill distinct from the selected day's solid one.
pairs.why: They answer different questions — where am I, and what did I pick. Merged, the calendar appears to have chosen for you.

pairs.dont: Hardcode Sunday or Monday as the first column.
pairs.why: People read the grid by shape as much as by number, and a week starting on the wrong day is misread rather than re-read.

a11y: react-day-picker owns the grid semantics, the roving focus and arrow-key movement. Do not re-implement them.
Only the chevron glyph is overridden, and it is aria-hidden — the navigation buttons take their names from react-day-picker, so changing its locale changes them.
Disabled days keep pointer-events-none and fg/disabled but stay in the accessibility tree, which is what lets someone discover a date is unavailable rather than just failing to reach it.
